source_title: Michael Douglas Says He Was Seen as a ‘Television Actor’ for Years Despite Being an Oscar-Winning Producer - People.com
source_excerpt:
Douglas said the studio initially rejected him from his 1984 film ‘Romancing the Stone’
ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty; Gary Gershoff/Getty
Michael Douglas opened up about the hard time he had getting cast in films, despite his Oscar for producing
Douglas was best known for the TV series The Streets of San Francisco even after he won an Oscar for One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest
Douglas finally cast himself in 1984’s Romancing the Stone after other actors turned the part down
Michael Douglas will always be grateful he got to star in 1984’s Romancing the Stone .
Douglas, 82, opened up about the movie in an Oct. 26 interview with GQ . In the video, he revisited some of his most iconic roles, including his leading role in Romancing the Stone as the brash Jack T. Colton. But because Douglas was best known for his work on TV, the studios wouldn’t initially confirm him to star in the film.
“I had done four seasons on Streets of San Francisco , which was a big television hit,” he said. He starred on The Streets of San Francisco from 1972 to 1976. He left the show in its fifth season to produce One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest . That movie, he noted, won him an Oscar for Best Picture.
“So now I was a movie producer,” he said. In 1979, he produced The China Syndrome , which he had a small role in. “I had offices at Columbia Studios and somebody brought me in this script called Romancing the Stone by a young woman named Diane Thomas, who was working as a waitress out at Alice’s restaurant in Malibu.”
The movie was “just magical,” he remembered. “It was a romantic adventure comedy with action, almost a mix that was very hard to come by.” He found a director in Robert Zemeckis , who, at the time, was worried “his directing career was over” because his first two pictures hadn’t worked. He loved the script too and signed on.
ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty
The next step was casting. “I never thought of myself of playing Jack Colton,” Douglas said. He thought the character would be more like Burt Reynolds in Deliverance , “a little more rugged guy,” he said. They initially wanted Debra Winger , who had starred in An Officer and a Gentleman , for the part of romance novelist Joan Wilder, but it didn’t work out. Instead, they cast Kathleen Turner , who had just finished Body Heat with William Hurt .
But then they had to cast Jack. “I tried to get a couple of the big actors to do it,” he said, but they all turned him down.
“The big issue I guess of making it was so funny that I’m an Academy Award-winning producer, but as an actor, I was a television actor trying to make the move into feature films,” he said. “So there were a lot of studios that did not approve me as an actor.” Though Douglas had film roles to his name, including 1971’s Summertree and 1979’s Running , none had been a real hit.

He remembered that when he was producing 1984’s Starman , he wanted to play the lead role, but, “I was not an approved actor in a film.” They gave the role to Jeff Bridges instead.
“But eventually they took a chance on me with Kathleen,” he said.
The actual production of the movie “was horrendously difficult and hard,” he said, as they filmed on location in Mexico. “I have the greatest respect for Kathleen because I couldn’t think of any other actress who had gone through all that she went through. So, she was a great, great asset to the film,” he said.
Romancing the Stone was a hit, making over $115 million at the box office. It received positive reviews from critics, helping make Douglas a movie star. Douglas and Turner also reunited to star in the 1985 sequel to Romancing the Stone , titled The Jewel of the Nile , and in 1989’s The War of the Roses . Turner also appeared on Douglas’ Netflix series The Kominsky Method , which ran from 2019 to 2021.
Earlier this month, Douglas revealed in his memoir One Helluva Ride that he and Turner, 72, had an affair while making the film.
“The chemistry I had with Kathleen Turner was so strong, audiences have been certain for years that we were in a relationship together while making the film,” Douglas wrote in his memoir , in an excerpt exclusively shared with PEOPLE. “We both denied it through Romancing the Stone , Jewel of the Nile , War of the Roses , and even while doing press a few years ago for The Kominsky Method .”
“The official story went as follows: Yes, we confessed, we had amazing chemistry. Yes, we were both, as Kathleen said, ‘terrible flirts,’’ and yes, we were both tempted, but nothing ever happened between us. That was a lie,” he wrote.
He said he “fell hard” for her. “We found each other first as friends, then as co-stars, and finally as lovers,” he said. Neither Zemeckis nor Danny DeVito ( Douglas’ long-time friend and his Romancing the Stone costar) knew.
Reacting to the book’s revelation about their relationship, Turner told PEOPLE in a statement, “Good heavens what a fuss about something 40 years ago! I love Michael and I look forward to enjoying the book.”
